articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran Designation Update
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a new Iran Designation Update on November 9, 2026.
Further details regarding the specific individuals or entities designated and the nature of the sanctions were not immediately available in the initial announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026.
The announcement did not immediately specify the individuals or entities targeted by these new sanctions, nor the precise nature of the prohibited activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities for Cyber, Transnational Crime, and Cuba-Related Activities
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations targeting cyber-related activities, transnational criminal organizations, and entities linked to Cuba on November 5, 2026.

As part of this action, OFAC published a Cuba-related Determination pursuant to Section 2(a)(i)(A) of Executive Order 14404, specifically targeting the 'Electronics, Manufacturing, Marine, and Technology Sectors of the Cuban Economy.'

Several individuals were added to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, including Kok Wa Chui from Madagascar, and Yujing He, Visal Pang, and Yong Qiu, all linked to Cambodia and the 'PRINCE GROUP TRANSNATIONAL CRIMINAL ORGANIZATION.'

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran-Related Designations, Venezuela GL, and Iran Alert
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates to existing listings on November 4, 2026.
OFAC also published an Iran-related Alert titled 'Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion,' highlighting deceptive practices used to circumvent sanctions.

Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License 5AA, authorizing certain transactions related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 Percent Bond on or after December 18, 2026, and an amended Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 595).

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.

The specific details of the amendments to the general license were not immediately provided in the announcement, but such actions typically clarify or adjust authorized activities under existing sanctions programs.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Linked to North Korea and DRC
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) on October 28, 2026.
These designations include individuals and entities tied to Russia, North Korea, and Rwanda, with several entries carrying restrictions under the North Korea Sanctions Regulations.
Among the designated entities is FIRST FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENT CENTER, located in North Korea and Vladivostok, Russia, identified as operating in financial and insurance activities.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, on October 27, 2026.
Extreme Networks agreed to pay $1,529,685 to resolve nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The violations involved the export of networking equipment and services between September 2018 and March 2022 to Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer that was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by designated entity JSC Concern Almaz Antey.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) amended several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026, as part of its ongoing review of published guidance.
The updated FAQs, including numbers 10, 32-36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, cover topics such as blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.

These revisions aim to ensure that information remains current and provide clarity on compliance procedures, particularly regarding when to block versus reject transactions and the proper format and timing for reporting.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026.
Concurrently, OFAC also announced the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea.

The action included the issuance of new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, along with amended Frequently Asked Questions, indicating adjustments to authorized activities and guidance under these sanctions programs.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations and Associated General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.

As part of this action, OFAC issued PAIPA General License 1, 'Transactions Authorized Pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations,' and PAIPA General License 2, 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving Certain Entities Blocked on October 19, 2026.'

Several entities were added to OFAC's Non-SDN Menu Based Sanctions List, including BEIJING QIJI CHUANGTAN PHASE I VENTURE CAPITAL CENTER LIMITED PARTNERSHIP (a.k.a. MIRACLE PLUS RMB FUND I), which faces prohibitions on loans from U.S. financial institutions exceeding $10,000,000 in any 12-month period.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Fined Over $1.5 Million by OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations

The settlement addresses nine apparent violations involving the export of networking equipment and services to a Russian defense manufacturer that was a blocked person by operation of law.
OFAC determined that these apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed and egregious, leading to the significant civil penalty.

articles.headline: U.S. Consumer Prices Rise More Than Expected in October, Fueling Rate Hike Concerns
body: U.S. consumer prices increased by 0.4% in October, exceeding economists' expectations of a 0.3% rise, according to data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
This marks the third consecutive month of sharp increases in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), with shelter costs accounting for nearly a third of the overall monthly increase.

The persistent rise in prices, particularly beyond food and energy, suggests that inflation is broadening, leading to increased expectations for another Federal Reserve interest rate hike at its December monetary policy meeting.

articles.headline: China Extends Suspension of Sanctions and Export Controls on U.S. Companies
body: China's Ministry of Commerce announced an extension of the suspension of trade restrictions and countermeasures against 32 U.S.-linked companies and six strategic export control measures for another two months, effective November 10, 2026.

This decision, which includes measures against 16 U.S. companies on its Export Control List and 11 companies on its Unreliable Entity List, is intended to implement the consensus reached during the eighth round of China-U.S. economic and trade consultations.

While the suspensions offer a temporary reprieve, exporters seeking to supply the affected companies must still apply to the Ministry of Commerce for authorization, with licenses granted following regulatory review.

articles.headline: China Opposes U.S. Sanctions on Chinese Firms Over Cuba Links
body: China expressed strong opposition to U.S. sanctions imposed on two Chinese companies, China National Electronics Import & Export Corporation (CEIEC) and Beijing H&C Technologies Co. Ltd., on November 7, 2026.
The U.S. State Department announced the sanctions on November 5, alleging that the two firms supplied components and equipment to Cuba's military through a Cuban procurement firm.

Beijing views these unilateral measures as a violation of international law and a detriment to the legitimate interests of Chinese companies and the stability of bilateral economic relations, reserving the right to take necessary countermeasures.

articles.headline: BIS Extends Suspension of Affiliates Rule Until January 2027
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has extended the suspension of its Affiliates Rule for an additional two months, postponing the implementation of expanded export controls until January 10, 2027.

The Affiliates Rule, originally published on September 30, 2025, aimed to extend existing end-user restrictions to companies owned 50% or more, directly or indirectly, by entities on certain U.S. restricted-party lists.

This latest extension, effective November 9, 2026, provides further relief for exporters by delaying the requirement to apply these expanded ownership-based restrictions, though existing export control requirements for individually listed entities remain in force.

articles.headline: Department of Commerce Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced that, as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR).
This deregulatory action shifts control of these items from the State Department's U.S. Munitions List to the EAR, aligning their export controls with those already applied to firearms.
The change aims to streamline the export process for these items, potentially reducing administrative burdens for manufacturers and exporters.

articles.headline: Extension of the Suspension of Expansion of End-User Controls for Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
